officialTitle: Gefitinib or carboplatin-paclitaxel in pulmonary adenocarcinoma

design.notes: Clinically selected (not EGFR-selected) East Asian population of non-smokers or former light smokers with adenocarcinoma; EGFR mutation status analysed in a biomarker subgroup.

clinicalQuestion: In clinically selected East Asian never/light smokers with advanced pulmonary adenocarcinoma, is first-line gefitinib non-inferior to carboplatin-paclitaxel, and does EGFR mutation status predict benefit?

pico.population: Previously untreated East Asian patients with advanced pulmonary adenocarcinoma who were non-smokers or former light smokers
pico.outcomes: Primary: PFS (non-inferiority, then superiority). Biomarker subgroup analysis by EGFR mutation status

arms.label: Gefitinib
arms.doseSourceQuote: to receive gefitinib (250 mg per day) (609 patients)

arms.label: Carboplatin-paclitaxel
arms.dosing: Carboplatin AUC 5 or 6 plus paclitaxel 200 mg/m²
arms.doseSourceQuote: carboplatin (at a dose calculated to produce an area under the curve of 5 or 6 mg per milliliter per minute) plus paclitaxel (200 mg per square meter of body-surface area) (608 patients)

publications.title: Gefitinib or carboplatin-paclitaxel in pulmonary adenocarcinoma.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The 12-month rates of progression-free survival were 24.9% with gefitinib and 6.7% with carboplatin-paclitaxel. The study met its primary objective of showing the noninferiority of gefitinib and also showed its superiority, as compared with carboplatin-paclitaxel, with respect to progression-free survival in the intention-to-treat population (hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.85; P<0.001).

In the subgroup of 261 patients who were positive for the epidermal growth factor receptor gene (EGFR) mutation, progression-free survival was significantly longer among those who received gefitinib than among those who received carboplatin-paclitaxel (hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.36 to 0.64; P<0.001)

whereas in the subgroup of 176 patients who were negative for the mutation, progression-free survival was significantly longer among those who received carboplatin-paclitaxel (hazard ratio for progression or death with gefitinib, 2.85; 95% CI, 2.05 to 3.98; P<0.001)

safety.description: Most common adverse events with gefitinib: rash or acne; diarrhoea
safety.sourceQuote: The most common adverse events were rash or acne (in 66.2% of patients) and diarrhea (46.6%) in the gefitinib group

safety.description: Most common adverse events with carboplatin-paclitaxel: neurotoxicity, neutropenia, alopecia
safety.sourceQuote: neurotoxic effects (69.9%), neutropenia (67.1%), and alopecia (58.4%) in the carboplatin-paclitaxel group

strengths: Large randomised phase III trial with prespecified biomarker analysis
Demonstrated a qualitative interaction: benefit in EGFR-mutant and harm in EGFR wild-type tumours
limitations: Population selected clinically rather than by EGFR genotype; mutation status available only in a subset

clinicalImplications.text: Established EGFR mutation status, rather than clinical characteristics, as the key predictor of benefit from first-line EGFR TKI therapy, underpinning routine EGFR genotyping before first-line treatment of advanced adenocarcinoma.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Clinical enrichment is not a substitute for genotyping: in EGFR wild-type tumours, gefitinib was worse than chemotherapy for PFS.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 19692680. OS and EGFR subgroup updates not ingested.
